summary: Three sections that climb from concepts to practice. Section A asks short 'explain why' questions on the basics (comparability and consistency, the accrual basis, the five elements). Section B gives one month of transactions for a small trading firm and asks short questions on how specific items are treated (owner's capital, an asset bought on loan, interest not yet paid, closing stock). Section C is a 10-mark case: journal entries and ledger posting, a trial balance, and the effect of each transaction on the accounting equation. Calculators are allowed and answers must be in sequence.
paper_format: MST Fall 2026 (5 Sep 2026): 8 questions, all compulsory, answer in sequence (Q1 to Q8 or Q8 to Q1) or lose 5 marks. Section A (CO1, Apply): Q1 to Q3, 5 marks each. Section B (CO2, Apply): Q4 to Q7 on a 21-line transactions table (2, 2, 2, 4 marks). Section C (CO3, Analyze and Evaluate): Q8 case worth 10 marks (4 + 2 + 4).
question_verbs: Discuss with respect to the definitions
Why is this credited to ... instead of
At what amount should ... appear, and why?
Journalise, post to ledger, prepare a trial balance
Analyse the impact on the accounting equation
marks_structure: 5-mark concept: define the idea, explain why it matters, show it with a short example
2-mark treatment question: name the concept, state the correct treatment and the amount
4-mark valuation question: a working (cost per unit) plus the rule for choosing the value
10-mark case: journal entries with ledger posting (4), trial balance (2), accounting equation table for every transaction (4)
repeated_topics: Accrual basis and the matching principle
The five elements: position (assets, liabilities, equity) and performance (income, expenses)
Assets bought partly on loan, and accrued interest
Journal, ledger, trial balance and the accounting equation
sources: Photos of the printed MST paper, FA5201, Fall 2026 (5 Sep 2026), 3 pages
